scope: Pinned source only: whether the fixed-size FT key event can echo a per-request identity through the existing daemon and remote R0KH path

driver: common/ft.c:1751 zero-initializes automatic key request; 1767 emits full key element
ap/ap_ftkd.c:506 copies full event payload; 757 emits the response key element; 824 parses element after InitVec; 888 performs MAC-only lookup; 910-913 reset counters and complete ack_r1kh
common/ft.c:1517-1572 mutates key response fields in place and does not write reserved fields
include/ft.h:85 defines KeyInfo.RSV[4]; include/ft.h:238 defines key-element RSV[3]
common/ft_iocl.c:540 zeroes KeyInfo.RSV for the separate manual ioctl request
daemon_archive: trunk/user/ralinkiappd/rtmpiapp.c:3464 copies complete request payload into security block
trunk/user/ralinkiappd/rtmpiapp.c:2340 copies received InitVec and full security block to request OID
trunk/user/ralinkiappd/rtmpiapp.c:3574 copies complete response payload into ACK security block
trunk/user/ralinkiappd/rtmpiapp.c:2140-2151 packages InitVec and sends response OID to all registered Wi-Fi interfaces

round_trip: common/ft.c zero-initializes FT_KDP_EVT_KEY_ELM and emits the full fixed-size structure for automatic KEY_REQ
FT_KDP_EventInform copies the complete event payload; daemon SecurityBlockSend copies that payload unchanged into the security block
R0KH daemon passes the received key structure to FT_KDP_KeyRequestToUs; FT_QueryKeyInfoForKDP updates response fields in place and the response event copies the full structure
daemon SecurityBlockAck copies the complete returned structure and the response OID carries it back to the R1KH driver
ap_ftkd.c parses a leading eight-byte InitVec followed by FT_KDP_EVT_KEY_ELM, but the response handler does not compare the InitVec

available_fixed_size_identity.observed_writes: No writes to either reserved field in automatic request construction, FT_QueryKeyInfoForKDP, or FT_KDP_KeyRequestToUs; the manual ioctl path zeroes KeyInfo.RSV and is separate.
available_fixed_size_identity.candidate: Carry an opaque per-attempt token in these seven reserved bytes, with the BSS/MAC/WCID/association-generation context retained in a local pending-request ledger. Validate the token and context before key-cache mutation or completion.
available_fixed_size_identity.compatibility_boundary: Exact pinned c25283e path preserves the same structure in place and sends its full size. Other or older R0KH implementations are not verified; a missing or changed token must fail closed. No wire-size or daemon ABI change is proposed.

response_handler_current_behavior: lookup is by station MAC only
cache-miss counters reset and ack_r1kh completion occur after that lookup
no token, BSS, association-generation, or request-instance validation is present
ack_r1kh is initialized nowhere in pinned source, although native insertion zeroes the entry and the R1KH_HARD_RETRY path waits/completes it

verification.reserved_field_write_search: Only the unrelated manual ioctl request writes KeyInfo.RSV, setting it to zero; no automatic responder write found. The same source search found no RTMP_OS_INIT_COMPLETION call for ack_r1kh; only the wait, complete and close operations exist.

next: Prototype a token ledger with single-claim, timeout/association retirement, exact BSS+MAC+WCID+generation matching, and a response-side lease that can complete while the original AUTH handler is waiting. Then compose and target-compile ap_ftkd.c and all four existing FT TUs with the hard-retry variant.
